classification.difficultyReason: Identify matching vertices and an appropriate congruence test, supplying the common side in the joined figure, then infer the requested corresponding measurement.

content.prompt: If possible, write down a congruence statement (with the appropriate congruence test) in each part. Then find the value of $x$ or $\theta$, giving reasons. Keep the vertices written in matching order.

spec.description: Paired triangles RST and JKL, with all printed vertex labels, angle values, side labels and double side ticks retained. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: RS=10 cm; angle RST=70 degrees; angle RTS=30 degrees; ST=JK; angle KJL=30 degrees; angle JKL=70 degrees; KL=x.

answer.short:
$\triangle SRT\equiv\triangle KLJ$ (AAS); $x=10\text{ cm}$.

Matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle RST=\angle JKL=70^\circ$, $\angle RTS=\angle KJL=30^\circ$, and $ST=KJ$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle SRT\equiv\triangle KLJ$ (AAS).

$KL=SR$ because matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.

$$x=10\text{ cm}$$

spec.description: Joined triangles APQ and BPQ share PQ. Three ticks mark AP and PB; two ticks mark AQ and QB. The two adjacent angles at Q retain their separate labels.
spec.mathematics: AP=BP; AQ=BQ; PQ is common; angle AQP=theta; angle PQB=80 degrees.

answer.short:
$\triangle APQ\equiv\triangle BPQ$ (SSS); $\theta=80^\circ$.

Matching angles of congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked:
$AP=BP$ and $AQ=BQ$ (given), and $PQ=PQ$ (common side).

Therefore $\triangle APQ\equiv\triangle BPQ$ (SSS).

$\angle AQP=\angle BQP$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal.

$$\theta=80^\circ$$

spec.description: Paired triangles FBC and MUS retain vertex order, equal-side ticks, the two 35-degree givens in each triangle, BC=6 m and US=x.
spec.mathematics: Angle BFC=angle BCF=angle UMS=angle MSU=35 degrees; FC=MS; BC=6 m; US=x.

answer.short:
$\triangle FBC\equiv\triangle MUS$ (AAS); $x=6\text{ m}$.

Matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle BFC=\angle UMS=35^\circ$, $\angle BCF=\angle MSU=35^\circ$, and $FC=MS$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle FBC\equiv\triangle MUS$ (AAS).

$US=BC$ because matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.

$$x=6\text{ m}$$
